title: Merge of a graph generation onto the generation a peer published meanwhile
description: A builder plans and computes against its BASE generation and publishes by compare-and-swap of the pointer. When the swap is lost because peers published (the HEAD is newer), the delta of the builder is merged onto the head instead of being thrown away, by optimistic concurrency control with backward validation against everything published since the base. THEIRS are the owners whose manifest row differs between base and head; OURS are the owners whose manifest row the builder changed plus the project owners its fact index patch writes (upserts, drops, appends). The merge is refused (and the builder computes again from the head, as before) when: the head has another identity or implementation, or no manifest (`identity`, `head`); a peer changed the stub of an owner (`stubFields`: presence, root, kind, targets, configuration, native root, tag), which every computation reads, or the builder changed the stub of one of its own owners (added, removed or re-shaped a project) while a peer changed any owner, whose computation read the old stubs (`structure`); the head carries another environment, or a merged owner would keep edges of another environment than the published one (`environment`); an owner of OURS is in THEIRS or its fact rows differ between base and head (`owner`); both sides changed the global fragment differently (`global`); both sides changed the membership differently (`membership`); the merged index holds a derived fact no pseudo owner supports (`derived`); `rounds` swaps were lost. Otherwise the merged manifest is the head's owners with OURS replaced, the fact index is the head's index with the builder's patch applied again, where a pseudo owner (`envOwner` and every derived owner, whose name is the digest of its answer) keeps the union of both supports (more observations can only make a later verification stricter); the global fragment and the membership are taken from the side that changed them; the verified stamp unites the builder's covered owners without THEIRS and the head's covered owners at the older of the two times.
